messages:
maria: Quick sync 1: inline errors vs a compact right-hand summary for long console forms. Also re-evaluating destructive confirms: typed-confirm vs checkbox+undo. Short thoughts? alex: I prefer inline for instant feedback, but a right-rail summary after submit helps when errors are off-screen. Hybrid seems best. leah: Agreed on hybrid: validate on blur inline; if submit fails, show compact summary pinned to right with anchors. Keyboard accessible. sam: A11y essentials: summary must announce via aria-live and be tabbable. Each anchor should focus the field and set aria-describedby. Example snippet we reuse: ```
\n We couldn't save 1 errors.\n
``` jordan: Required-field markers: avoid asterisk-only. Use explicit "Required" helper for important fields, faint asterisk elsewhere, and never rely on color alone. maria: For destructive actions: three tiers: low-risk modal; mid-risk checkbox+undo (10s); high-risk short typed-confirm (type "DELETE"). Keep typed input short. alex: Implementation note: when summary anchor clicked, smooth-scroll and focus field. Expose inline message and add small animation to reduce context jump. leah: Test plan: keyboard navigation, SR announce on submit, contrast check for markers, focus management when jumping from summary. I'll draft checklist. aria-bot: Preview: https://staging.redwood.ai/console/ux/validation-hybrid - feature flag enabled. maria: Action items: alex -> SideErrorSummary PR; leah -> a11y checklist; sam -> add e2e aria-live assertion; jordan -> 5-person hallway test Monday. We'll iterate on copy in the doc. :thumbsup:
